questions.question: Three consecutive closing prices are 10, 12, and 14. What is the three-period simple moving average of those closes?
questions.explanation: Add the three closing prices and divide by three: (10 + 12 + 14) ÷ 3 = 12.
questions.learningObjective: Explain or apply simple moving averages.

questions.question: The next close is 16. For the series 10, 12, 14, 16, what is the latest three-period simple moving average?
questions.explanation: Use only the latest three closes: (12 + 14 + 16) ÷ 3 = 14. The oldest observation, 10, drops out.

questions.question: Compared with a five-period simple moving average, a fifty-period simple moving average generally does what?
options: Smooths more short-term variation and reacts more slowly
Responds instantly to every price change
Gives all weight to the newest close
Removes all uncertainty from the signal
questions.explanation: A longer average uses more observations, which smooths short-term fluctuations but usually increases lag.

questions.question: A chart has successive higher swing highs and higher swing lows. Which description best fits that structure?
options: A guaranteed reversal tomorrow
An uptrend
A price series with no trend
A downtrend
questions.explanation: Higher highs and higher lows are a common way to describe an upward price trend. The pattern does not guarantee future gains.

questions.question: In technical analysis, a support area is most commonly associated with which behavior?
options: Selling pressure repeatedly halts advances
Buying interest may interrupt a decline
Prices can never trade below the area
Every trade executes at exactly one price
questions.explanation: Support describes an area where buying interest may counter selling. It is an observed area, not a guarantee or permanent price floor.
questions.learningObjective: Explain or apply support and resistance.

questions.question: A resistance area is most commonly associated with which behavior?
options: The company has suspended all trading
Prices are legally prevented from rising
Buying interest repeatedly halts declines
Selling pressure may interrupt an advance
questions.explanation: Resistance describes an area where selling pressure may limit an advance. Prices can still move through it.
questions.learningObjective: Explain or apply support and resistance.

questions.question: Under the traditional 70/30 RSI convention, an RSI reading of 75 is usually described as what?
options: A certain sell signal
Oversold
Overbought
Exactly neutral
questions.explanation: A reading above 70 is traditionally called overbought. This label alone does not establish when a reversal will occur.

questions.question: RSI remains above 70 during a strong upward trend. Which interpretation is most defensible?
options: RSI must be broken because this is impossible
A price decline is certain on the next bar
Momentum can remain overbought for an extended period
The asset has no remaining risk
questions.explanation: RSI can stay at extreme readings during strong trends. Context matters; an overbought reading is not a precise reversal timetable.

questions.question: Compared with a simple moving average of the same period, how does an exponential moving average assign weights?
options: It weights only the oldest observation
It uses trading volume instead of prices
It assigns equal weight to every observation in the window
It places more weight on recent observations
questions.explanation: An EMA applies larger weights to more recent prices, generally making it more responsive than an equivalent-period SMA.
questions.learningObjective: Explain or apply exponential moving averages.

questions.question: A moving average drawn directly over the price chart is an example of which indicator presentation?
options: A company balance sheet
An exchange trading restriction
An overlay
A valuation forecast
questions.explanation: An overlay appears on the price chart itself. Oscillators such as RSI are commonly displayed in a separate panel.
